name: Coin Collector
camera_perspective: Fixed orthographic side view, camera perpendicular to the 2D plane showing the full play area.
art_style: Minimal flat solid-color shapes using Unity built-in sprites (white square/coin textures tinted) and simple UI Text. No textures, no external assets, no animations.
mechanics: Player moves left and right on flat ground
Collecting a coin increases score by 1
Win condition when all 5 coins collected
controls: Keyboard: Left/Right arrows or A/D to move left/right
Keyboard: Space or Up arrow to jump
Mobile: On-screen left and right touch buttons for movement
level_structure: Single flat green ground spanning the bottom of the screen. Five yellow coins placed above the ground at different horizontal positions and heights, all reachable by jumping. Player starts at a fixed position on the ground. No enemies, no obstacles, one level only.
ui_requirements: Score text displayed at top-left showing current score
Win text 'YOU WIN!' displayed centered when all 5 coins collected
Mobile touch buttons visible only on mobile platforms

requirements.original_instruction: create Create a very simple 2D mobile game called Coin Collector.
requirements.implementation: Set up a Unity 2D project with a single scene named MainGame. Configure the project for 2D and mobile build support. The game title is 'Coin Collector'.

requirements.original_instruction: The player is a blue square that moves left and right and jumps on a flat green ground.
requirements.implementation: Create a player GameObject as a blue square (SpriteRenderer with solid blue color) with Rigidbody2D and BoxCollider2D. Implement horizontal movement via velocity and jumping via vertical impulse when grounded. Create a flat green ground GameObject (SpriteRenderer with solid green color) with BoxCollider2D at the bottom of the screen.

requirements.original_instruction: Place 5 yellow coins above the ground.
requirements.implementation: Create 5 coin GameObjects, each a yellow circle (SpriteRenderer with solid yellow color and CircleCollider2D). Position them above the ground at varied horizontal and vertical positions, all reachable by jumping. Ensure they do not overlap the player start position.

requirements.original_instruction: Collecting a coin increases the score by 1 and removes the coin.
requirements.implementation: Implement OnTriggerEnter2D on the player to detect coin collisions. When a coin is collected, increment the score variable by 1, destroy the coin GameObject, and update the score UI text.

requirements.original_instruction: When all 5 coins are collected, display "YOU WIN!".
requirements.implementation: After each coin collection, check if score equals 5. If true, display a UI Text element with the exact text 'YOU WIN!' centered on the screen. Optionally stop player input.

requirements.original_instruction: Use only Unity built-in shapes, solid colors, and a simple text UI.
requirements.implementation: Use Unity's built-in Sprite shapes (white square and circle) tinted with solid colors via SpriteRenderer. Use Unity UI Text (Legacy) for score and win message. No external assets, no textures, no animations, no sound.

requirements.original_instruction: One scene, one level, no enemies, no textures, no external assets, no animations, and no sound.
requirements.implementation: Ensure the project contains exactly one scene (MainGame) and one level. Do not add enemies, textures, external assets, animations, or audio sources. All visuals are procedural built-in shapes.

requirements.original_instruction: Keep everything minimal, functional, and easy to test.
requirements.implementation: Use simple scripts with clear logic, expose movement speed and jump force as public variables for tuning. Ensure the game can be tested quickly in the Unity Editor with keyboard and on device with touch buttons.

requirements.original_instruction: Use keyboard controls for PC testing and simple touch buttons for mobile.
requirements.implementation: Implement input handling that reads keyboard (Left/Right arrows or A/D for movement, Space/Up for jump) on PC. On mobile, display three UI touch buttons (left, right, jump) that set the same movement and jump inputs. Use Unity's Input class and platform detection to enable/disable touch buttons.

tasks.description: Create Unity 2D project structure with single scene 'MainGame' and set up camera and basic settings.
Create player blue square GameObject with Rigidbody2D, BoxCollider2D, and movement/jump script.
Create flat green ground GameObject with BoxCollider2D and position it at the bottom.
Create 5 yellow coin GameObjects with CircleCollider2D and place them above ground at varied positions.
Implement coin collection logic: detect trigger, increment score, destroy coin, update UI.
Implement win condition: when score reaches 5, display 'YOU WIN!' text centered.
Create UI Canvas with score text (top-left) and win text (centered, initially hidden).
Implement keyboard input for movement and jump using Input.GetAxisRaw and Input.GetKeyDown.
Implement mobile touch buttons: create three UI buttons (left, right, jump) and wire them to set movement flags and trigger jump. Show only on mobile platforms.
Test the game in Unity Editor: verify player movement, jumping, coin collection, score update, and win message. Also verify touch buttons appear in mobile build.

assumptions: The game uses Unity's built-in Sprite shapes (white square and circle) tinted with solid colors via SpriteRenderer.
The player square size is 1x1 unit, ground is a long rectangle, coins are circles of diameter 0.8 units.
The camera is orthographic with size set to show a play area of about 12x7 units.
The player starts at a fixed position on the ground, e.g., (-4, 0.5).
Coins are placed at positions like (-3, 2), (-1, 3), (1, 2), (3, 3), (0, 4) to be reachable by jumping.
Gravity and jump force are tuned so the player can reach the highest coin.
Score UI is a legacy Text component at top-left; win text is centered.
Touch buttons are only active on mobile platforms; on PC they are hidden.
No pause, restart, or menu is required.
The game ends after displaying 'YOU WIN!' but the scene remains active.
All scripts are attached to appropriate GameObjects in the single scene.
The project uses Unity 2021 or later with 2D template.
No external assets or audio are used; all visuals are procedural.
The game is tested in landscape orientation on mobile.
The player cannot move beyond the screen edges; optional clamping is implemented.
limitations: No animations, textures, external assets, or sound are used as requested.
The game is minimal and does not include menus, restart, or additional levels.
Touch buttons are simple UI buttons without fancy styling.
The win condition is only triggered when all 5 coins are collected; no other win conditions.
The game does not handle multi-touch or complex input.
The player cannot die or lose; there is no fail state.
The game is not optimized for different screen aspect ratios; it assumes a fixed landscape view.
No save system or persistent data.
The game uses legacy UI Text for simplicity.
The game is not designed for accessibility or localization.
